Read the following excerpt from the driftctl command-line reference, then answer the question using only what the document says.

---
driftctl sync — reconcile a local snapshot directory with its remote peer.

Usage: driftctl sync [options] <snapshot-dir>

Network options:
  --peer <url>        Remote peer endpoint. Required unless DRIFTCTL_PEER is set.
  --timeout <n>       Per-request timeout in seconds. Default: 30 seconds.
  --retry-limit <n>   Maximum number of retry attempts after a failed transfer.
                      Default: 4. Set to 0 to fail immediately on the first error.
  --retry-backoff <n> Fixed pause between retry attempts. Default: 45 seconds.
                      driftctl does not use exponential backoff; the pause is
                      the same for every attempt.
  --parallel <n>      Number of concurrent transfer workers. Default: 8.

Exit codes: 0 on success, 3 when the retry budget is exhausted, 5 on a
local snapshot integrity failure. Transfers interrupted by SIGINT resume
from the last committed chunk on the next invocation.
---

Question: When a transfer fails, how does driftctl sync retry it? Name the two flags that control retrying and state the default value of the pause between attempts, including its unit.

Read the following excerpt from the packmule configuration reference, then answer the question using only what the document says.

---
packmule bundles build artifacts into content-addressed archives. Bundle
behaviour is controlled by the [bundle] table in packmule.toml.

[bundle]
codec        String. Compression codec applied to every archive member.
             One of "zstd", "lz4", or "none". Default: "zstd" at level 6.
             Level is fixed per codec and is not configurable.
max_size     String with unit. Upper bound on a single bundle file before
             packmule splits output into numbered parts. Default: "250 MB".
             Accepted units are MB and GB only.
dedup        Boolean. Content-level deduplication of identical members
             across bundles in the same store. This feature is
             disabled by default because it requires a store-wide index that grows with
             every bundle; enable it only on stores under 100k bundles.
sign         Boolean. Attach a detached signature to each part. Default:
             true when a signing key is configured, false otherwise.
---

Question: With a stock packmule.toml that sets nothing in the [bundle] table, which compression codec is used, at what size does output get split into parts, and is deduplication on or off? Quote the document's own wording for the dedup setting.

Read the following excerpt from the lumberd daemon manual, then answer the question using only what the document says.

---
lumberd is a single-binary log collector. Rotation is governed by the
[rotation] section of /etc/lumberd/lumberd.conf.

[rotation]
rotate_every   Duration. How often the active log file is closed and a new
               one opened, regardless of size. Default: 12 hours. The
               smallest accepted value is 15 minutes; sub-minute values are
               rejected at startup with exit code 2.
rotate_size    Size threshold that forces an early rotation. Default: 512 MB.
               Set to 0 to rotate on time alone.
keep_files     Integer. Number of rotated files retained before the oldest
               is deleted. Default: 9. The active file does not count
               toward this limit.
compress_old   Codec applied to a file when it is rotated out. The only
               supported codec is gzip; set to "off" to keep rotated files
               uncompressed. Default: gzip at level 5.
---

Question: Out of the box, on what schedule does lumberd rotate its active log file, and what happens to a file once it has been rotated out? Name the setting that controls the schedule, its default value with unit, and the compression codec applied to rotated files.
